title: fix(cloud-connection)!: a runtime holding the env service key is platform-managed: no Setup page, disconnect refused; the entry moves to Integrations
body:
Fixes #25097

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

Ruling 甲 (the maintainer, in the triage chat, as the card records it: 「一、云连接 甲」), the platform half. The pair objectstack-ai/cloud#3137 carries the hosted per-env kernel's own registration and is not touched here.

## What changes

A runtime is **platform-managed** when its effective control-plane credential is the environment service key (`controlPlaneApiKey`, or `OS_CLOUD_API_KEY`, which the cloud sets on the environments it hosts). `CloudConnectionPlugin` now reads that as one predicate, `platformManaged`, and the existing credential resolver is written in terms of it, so the two cannot disagree. It is used in two places:

- **Registration.** A managed runtime does not register the Cloud Connection UI bundle, so neither the `cloud_connection_settings` page nor the `nav_cloud_connection` entry is served. It logs one `info` line at boot saying so.
- **Disconnect.** A managed runtime refuses a disconnect with `409` `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`. The refusal comes after the sign-in, held-session and Setup Access checks, which keep their answers and their order, and before the control-plane revoke and the local credential clear. The message names the platform as the connection's manager and offers no remedy, because the runtime has none to offer.

Everywhere else (self-hosted or local, connected through the device-code flow), the page and disconnect are unchanged. The nav entry moves from `group_apps` to `group_integrations`. It keeps priority 200, which sorts it last there. The other entries' priorities, read where they are declared: Webhooks and HTTP Deliveries (`plugin-webhooks`) 100, Datasources (`service-datasource`) 100, Connect an Agent (`mcp`) 110. Measured once on a merged Setup app with Cloud Connection registered first: `group_integrations` served `nav_webhooks, nav_http_deliveries, nav_datasources, nav_connect_agent, nav_cloud_connection`.

**Error code, and the precedent followed.** `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` / 409 is the standard catalog's 409 member. No code is minted, on the rule this plugin's own `SETUP_ACCESS_REFUSAL` (`PERMISSION_DENIED`) already follows: the ADR-0112 ledger sends a generic condition to the standard catalog rather than registering a synonym. It is also the answer this package's install-local door gives for a refusal that comes from runtime state rather than from the request (the writable-base namespace conflict). A dedicated code would need a ledger entry under `packages/spec`, which is out of this lane. `error-envelope.conformance.test.ts` gains the case.

## Contract

Every input whose answer changes, before and after. Nothing else moves: the connection status answer is unchanged on every runtime, and bind start and bind poll are unchanged.

| Input | Before | After |
|:--|:--|:--|
| A disconnect request on a runtime holding the service key, from a signed-in caller holding Setup Access | The control plane was asked to revoke the connection. The stored device credential was cleared. The answer was success, and status went on reading bound, because the key stayed in use. | Refused: `409` `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` in the declared envelope, with a message naming the platform as the connection's manager. Nothing is revoked or cleared. |
| The same request from a caller with no session, a held session or no Setup Access | 401, the gate's 403 or `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403 | Unchanged, and still answered first |
| The page listing on a runtime holding the service key | serves `cloud_connection_settings` | does not serve it |
| Setup's merged navigation on a runtime holding the service key | `nav_cloud_connection` in `group_apps` | no `nav_cloud_connection` anywhere |
| Setup's merged navigation on a runtime without the key | `nav_cloud_connection` in `group_apps`, an ungated group | `nav_cloud_connection` in `group_integrations`, last. That group requires `manage_platform_settings`, so a caller holding Setup Access without it (the default `organization_admin` set) no longer sees the entry. The connect and disconnect requests still take Setup Access alone. |
| The boot log of a runtime holding the service key | nothing about the page | one `info` line: platform-managed, page and entry not registered, disconnecting refused |
| Exported `CLOUD_CONNECTION_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS` / `CLOUD_CONNECTION_UI_BUNDLE` | `group: 'group_apps'` | `group: 'group_integrations'` (same type, same priority, same item) |

The claim's Clause-② basis said the nav move "only regroups an entry". As measured, it also narrows who is served the entry on a runtime without the key: that is the fifth row. The row narrows a served answer, so the declaration stays `no (narrowing)`.

**Changeset level.** The card says `patch`. The changeset grades `minor`. AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist step 3) reads "`(narrowing)` is BREAKING". The header of `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` reads "During the launch window we ship breaking changes as `minor`". All 19 pending changesets that carry `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` grade their primary package `minor`. The fixed group already holds pending `minor` stock, so the next release's version number does not move. The changeset carries the Clause-② line, a **BREAKING** banner, and an ADR-0087 disposition of not-required (no-migration-prescription). The level axis stands down on a `no` declaration.

## Tests

New pin: `packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-platform-managed.pin.test.ts`, 8 cases.

- Registration, read back from a real `ObjectKernel` + `ObjectQLPlugin` through the metadata protocol. Managed through `controlPlaneApiKey` and through `OS_CLOUD_API_KEY`: no page, and no `nav_cloud_connection` anywhere in Setup's tree. Not managed: the page is served and the entry is the only child of `group_integrations`, absent from `group_apps`. Each reading has a lit control in the same composition: a control page that IS served, and `nav_marketplace_browse` in `group_apps`.
- Boot log: exactly one line naming the platform-managed state.
- Disconnect, both resolution modes. Managed: `409` `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, `BaseResponseSchema` + `envelopeViolations` + `ApiErrorSchema` all clean, and the message's first sentence pinned. The control plane gets zero calls, so no revoke, and the stored credential is untouched. Control, not managed: exactly one call, the revoke, and the credential is cleared.

**Red then green.** Run against `origin/main`'s plugin (`5050442bb`): 6 failed, 2 passed (the two not-managed disconnect controls). After the fix: 8 passed. Hash-equal ablation at `adac487886`: both source files restored to their `5050442bb` blobs (`233061ff…`, `d84ed969…`, landing verified by `git hash-object`), then 5 suites run. Result: 10 failed, 69 passed, and every failure is a new assertion. Restored to the HEAD blobs (`be039a06…`, `beffc3d7…`) by `git checkout HEAD --`, with `git diff HEAD` empty and status clean.

**Existing pins, what each asserts and what changed:**

- `cloud-connection-auth-gate.pin.test.ts`: the UN-HELD control ("the same caller is served by all seven doors") ran on the service-key mount, where disconnect is now the 409. It now reads both shapes: self-hosted (all seven served, disconnect driven last because it really clears the credential the other doors present), and managed (six served, disconnect is the 409 with no control-plane call). HELD cases are unchanged.
- `cloud-connection-setup-access.pin.test.ts`: the CONTROL ("a setup.access holder is served by all three doors") likewise reads both shapes. Bind start and bind poll keep every prior assertion in both. Disconnect is served in the self-hosted shape, and in the managed shape it is the 409 with the credential kept. The 403 refusals are unchanged and still run on the managed mount, so they still prove the 403 precedes the 409.
- `marketplace-installed-ui-entry.pin.test.ts`: its "plugin absent" control used `nav_cloud_connection` as the plugin-contributed entry in `group_apps`. That entry left the group, so the control is now `nav_marketplace_browse` (the browse bundle is registered in the composition), and the shell gains the `group_integrations` anchor. The page-listing control (`cloud_connection_settings` served) is unchanged.
- `packages/cli/test/platform-page-i18n-parity.test.ts` (plugin page i18n parity, read from the static bundle), `packages/cli/scripts/check-app-nav-i18n.mjs` (every merged Setup/Account nav id labelled in every locale), `packages/qa/dogfood/test/platform-app-object-entry-views.test.ts` (object entries' first list view): unchanged and green. Translation keys are per app and nav id (`apps.setup.navigation.nav_cloud_connection`), so the regroup changes none: `check:app-nav-i18n` OK, 12 contributors, setup 52 merged ids.

At `b5445185dd` (the final commit): `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cloud-connection exec vitest run`, 54 files / 637 tests passed. `typecheck` exit 0. The three cross-package pins above were re-run green at the same commit (27, 49, and `check:app-nav-i18n` OK).

## Docs that the change would otherwise falsify

- `content/docs/deployment/cloud-connection.mdx`: Setup, Integrations, Cloud Connection paths; a managed server has no entry and refuses to disconnect; the entry's group gate; the reference row for the disconnect request.
- `content/docs/ui/setup-app.mdx`: the Apps and Integrations rows.
- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/platform-core.json`: `platform-core.marketplace-console-honesty` steps[3] and acceptance[0] re-pointed, revision 6.

## Acceptance notes

Noted, not filed:

- On a managed runtime, bind start and bind poll still run. A completed device bind there would persist a device credential that is never presented, because the service key wins. The binding flow is held off for this card, and with no page, nothing in the product reaches those requests on a managed runtime. Carrier: none.
- `content/docs/ui/setup-app.mdx` was already missing Datasources (`service-datasource`) and Connect an Agent (`mcp`) from the Integrations row. Pre-existing doc drift, not widened here. Carrier: none.
- Measured on `origin/main` (Zone 2 of the dispatch). Status reads bound on a runtime holding the key, both when the control plane answers not-bound and when it is down. A disconnect there asked the control plane to revoke the connection, emptied the stored token, and status still read bound afterwards.

## Gates

Read at `b5445185dd` (the final commit). `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 97 commands. Each was run with its exit code captured before any pipe: all 97 exit 0. The 10 families under "Declared WIDE population" were also run: all exit 0. Reconciliation: "Run reconciliation — 97 derived, 97 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN." `pnpm lint` (the whole-repo `eslint . --no-inline-config`): exit 0 at `b5445185dd`, no output. It ran with a 6 GB heap rather than 4 GB, to give the whole-repo scan headroom.
